rationale: Round-2 classification of my six round-1 asks, re-derived by re-reading each target file at tip 0783a507 rather than trusting the commit message. Four are cleanly ADDRESSED (F1, F2, F3, F6), one is ADDRESSED and went further than I asked (F4), and one is PARTIAL (F5). The sweep was done well: F4's fix not only added the writer I named but also added the v2-translation writer I had not caught, and applied the identical correction to internal/phase/phaselock.go's header, which carried the same defect plus seven stale line citations. I re-derived the writer set independently at the tip — the ten non-test WithPhaseWriteLock call sites (next.go, repair.go, adopt.go, impl.go, plan.go, spec.go, complete.go, migrate.go, sanctioned_sync.go, semantics_v2.go) now match both enumerations exactly, and phaselock.go correctly notes release.go reaches the lock via SanctionedDerivedSync rather than directly. F1's new runbook text is confirmed against the code at the tip: runMaterialization still gates doc-sync (materialize.go:374-378) before CheckADRDivergenceSnapshot/handleADRGateOutcome (:380-386), so the sequential-gates consequence the runbook now states is true, and it now agrees with merge-safety.md's two-retry contract instead of contradicting it. F6 is correct in both places against gitutil/materialize.go:238's actual `git reset --quiet --mixed HEAD`. The agreement-table cross-pin test is green at the tip after the lifecycle-modes.md edits (go test ./internal/phase -run TestAgreementTable -short: ok, 130s), so the verbatim cell parser was not disturbed by the prose changes above the table markers. Two items remain open, both MINOR, both doc-only, both one-line edits. N1 is a NEW_ISSUE the round-1 fix introduced: core/architecture.md now attributes advancePhaseOnClaim to bead 7, which git falsifies (it was introduced by 798841b9, 'impl(mindspec-ta30.2)', and hardened by 542992b4, bead 2's own round-1 panel fix), and it contradicts phaselock.go:9's 'bead 2's OQ-3 writer' — corrected in the very same commit. I want to own this plainly: 'bead 7' came from MY round-1 F4 text, where I mis-assigned the b2<->b7 seam's two halves; the fixer independently got it right in phaselock.go and wrong only where they followed my wording. F5 is PARTIAL because the fix corrected the leg criterion exactly as asked, but retargeted the antecedent of the very next sentence: 'each of those eight rows' canonical fixture inputs are hardcoded ... (never copied from the row record)' now points at the seven-ordinary-plus-forced-backward set, and row 12's fixture does copy from the record (rowRepairPhaseForcedBackward seeds 'mindspec_phase': row.derivation). There are two distinct eights here and the fix crossed them. Neither item touches code correctness, neither needs a re-panel, and both are sentence-level corrections; I file REQUEST_CHANGES only because they are factually wrong statements in landed docs of exactly the class this spec exists to close, not because the branch is unsound. One honest gap: I could not re-run `mindspec validate docs` in round 2 — the Bash tool became unavailable (safety-classifier outage) after my test run. My six items are prose and doc-comment edits that cannot affect that gate's source-glob/ownership/doc-sync checks, it was clean at round 1, and the BRIEF reports it clean at this tip; I am reporting the gap rather than implying I re-confirmed it.
concrete_changes_required: N1 (NEW_ISSUE, introduced by the round-1 fix) -- .mindspec/domains/core/architecture.md:185: the parenthetical '(`cmd/mindspec/next.go`'s `advancePhaseOnClaim` — the bead-7 writer this spec itself added, classified forward-by-intent in lifecycle-modes.md's writer taxonomy)' names the wrong bead. `git log -S"func advancePhaseOnClaim" -- cmd/mindspec/next.go` gives 798841b9 'impl(mindspec-ta30.2): OQ-3 option-1 phase semantics + v2 reconciliation' (with 542992b4, bead 2's round-1 panel fix, hardening it) — bead 2, not bead 7. internal/phase/phaselock.go:9, corrected in the SAME commit, already says 'bead 2's OQ-3 writer', so the two documents now disagree. Cheapest correct fix: change 'the bead-7 writer' to 'the bead-2 writer', or simply delete the four-word bead attribution (the enumeration does not need provenance — phaselock.go carries it). Provenance note so this is not re-researched: the 'bead 7' error originated in MY round-1 F4 text, not in the fixer's own analysis; I mis-split the BRIEF's b2<->b7 seam, whose halves are bead 2's claim-advance and bead 7's absent-only spec-approve backfill.

F5 (PARTIAL) -- project-docs/user/guides/lifecycle-modes.md, the paragraph at lines ~23-37: the leg criterion is now correct ('for the seven ordinary three-surface rows plus the forced-backward row'), but the sentence that follows still reads 'each of those eight rows' canonical fixture inputs are hardcoded to the real verb's own write semantics in the Go source (never copied from the row record)', and its antecedent is now that leg set — for which the claim is false at row 12. rowRepairPhaseForcedBackward (agreement_table_test.go:844+) builds its post-epic with Metadata['mindspec_phase'] = row.derivation, i.e. copied from the record; its independence rests instead on two pre-use setup guards (DerivePhaseFromChildren against independently-fixed children, and IsBackwardMove(preStored, freshDerived)). Two different eights exist in this fixture file and the fix crossed them: the HARDCODED-STORED-LITERAL set is the seven ordinary rows plus the TERMINAL row (agreement_table_test.go's own header: 'The terminal row's derivation input is decoupled the same way (hardcoded state.ModeDone...)'), while the DERIVEPHASEFROMCHILDREN-LEG set is the seven ordinary rows plus the FORCED-BACKWARD row. Fix by decoupling the two sentences — e.g. keep the corrected leg-set phrasing where it is, and change 'each of those eight rows' to 'each of the seven ordinary rows' and the terminal row's', then note that the forced-backward row's independence comes from its two setup guards rather than a hardcoded stored literal.
